claims.evidence: No shipping documents or port stickers are visible in the report.
Photo 0 shows significant dirt and brown residue on the engine block and components.
Mechanical operation cannot be determined from a static photo of an uninstalled engine.
The seller provides conflicting origins (America vs Belgium) and no customs documentation is shown.
Mileage is not recorded on the engine itself.
Requires close-up photos of factory seals and bolt heads to verify.

risks.risk: Internal sludge or poor maintenance history.
risks.proof: A clear photo of the underside of the oil filler cap and the visible valvetrain inside.
risks.if_unproven: As a high-mileage unit requiring internal cleaning.

risks.risk: Locally used engine being sold as imported (Tokunbo).
risks.proof: Original Bill of Lading or Nigerian Customs clearing documents matching the engine serial.

risks.risk: Internal mechanical failure (e.g., low compression or rod knock).
risks.proof: A video of a compression test or a cold start if mounted.
risks.if_unproven: As a non-running core for parts or rebuilding.

risks.risk: Missing or damaged sensors and wiring harness.
risks.proof: Detailed photos of all sides of the engine showing the harness and sensor plugs.
risks.if_unproven: As a bare long block without accessories.

proof_requests: Clear photo of the oil filler cap removed to check for sludge.
Photos of the engine serial number.
Customs clearance papers or Bill of Lading to verify 'Tokunbo' status.
Close-up photos of the cylinder head bolts to check if it has been opened.
response.reason: The item is clearly identified as a Toyota VVT-i engine. Due to the visible dirt and contradictory seller claims regarding origin, it is priced as a locally used unit in average condition.
